questions.q: What two columns does Unpivot Columns always produce from the columns you selected?
options: Attribute (the original column headers) and Value (what was under them)
Key and Data
Row and Column
Source and Target
questions.explain: Attribute holds the original column header names; Value holds the data that used to sit under each header — the standard attribute-value pair unpivot produces.

questions.q: Why is a "wide" table (one column per date) harder to work with than an unpivoted one?
options: The date is baked into column headers instead of being real, filterable data in a column
Wide tables can't be loaded into Power BI at all
Wide tables always contain errors
There is no real difference — it's purely a stylistic preference
questions.explain: When "which date" is a column header rather than a value, you can't easily filter, chart, or relate that information the way you can with a true column of data.

questions.q: What's the key advantage of Unpivot Other Columns over plain Unpivot Columns?
options: It automatically picks up new columns added to the source on future refreshes, since it unpivots everything except the columns you chose to keep
It runs faster
It produces a different, more compact output
It doesn't require selecting any columns at all
questions.explain: Unpivot Other Columns is defined by what to keep, not what to unpivot — so if the source later gains a new date column, it gets swept up automatically. Plain Unpivot Columns locks in the specific columns selected at the time.

options: The reverse of Unpivot — turns unique values from one column into new column headers, filled with another column's values
It's another name for Unpivot Columns
It deletes duplicate rows
It merges two columns into one
questions.explain: Pivot Column takes a tall/unpivoted table and turns it back into a wide layout — unique values become new column headers.

questions.q: A source table gains a new date column and two new rows after a refresh. Which unpivot approach picks up the new column automatically?
options: Unpivot Other Columns
Unpivot Columns
Neither picks up new columns automatically
Both behave identically in this scenario
questions.explain: Unpivot Other Columns unpivots everything except the explicitly-kept columns, so a new date column gets included automatically. Plain Unpivot Columns only acts on the specific columns selected when the step was created.
